prompt: I'm setting up Scapy from a specific commit and want to understand how it works before diving into packet crafting. Can you start the Scapy shell and show me what the startup looks like? What version is it running? Then create a basic ICMP echo request and show me what fields get auto-populated in the IP header. What does the output look like when you call show() on it? Also, send a crafted ICMP packet to the localhost and describe what happens at the network layer as observed in Scapy. Additionally, explore the source code and explain how Scapy constructs the IP header by default when creating packets programmatically. Also, I want to run the test suite to make sure everything's working. How many tests are there and what does the pass/fail summary show? Don't modify any source files, if you need to create temp scripts, just clean them up after.

reference_answer:
Scapy’s interactive shell at this commit starts with an ASCII art banner and reports version 2.5.0.dev87. Run `scapy` to launch it. Here's exactly what you see:

```
                     aSPY//YASa       
             apyyyyCY//////////YCa       |
            sY//////YSpcs  scpCY//Pp     | Welcome to Scapy
ayp ayyyyyyySCP//Pp           syY//C    | Version 2.5.0.dev87
AYAsAYYYYYYYY///Ps              cY//S   |
         pCCCCY//p          cSSps y//Y   | https://github.com/secdev/scapy
         SPPPP///a          pP///AC//Y   |
              A//A            cyP////C   | Have fun!
              p///Ac            sC///a   |
              P////YCpc           A//A   | Craft packets like I craft my beer.
       scccccp///pSP///p          p//Y   |               -- Jean De Clerck
      sY/////////y  caa           S//P   |
       cayCyayP//Ya              pY/Ya
        sY/PsY////YCc          aC//Yp 
         sc  sccaCY//PCypaapyCP//YSs  
                  spCPY//////YPSps    
                       ccaacs         
                                       using IPython 9.4.0
```

When you create IP()/ICMP(), run `p = IP()/ICMP(); p.show()`—output before building shows these auto-populated fields:

```
###[ IP ]### 
  version   = 4
  ihl       = None        # Computed at build time
  tos       = 0x0
  len       = None        # Computed at build time  
  id        = 1
  flags     = 
  frag      = 0
  ttl       = 64          # Default TTL
  proto     = icmp        # Auto-set based on payload type
  chksum    = None        # Computed at build time
  src       = 127.0.0.1   # Auto-resolved from routing table
  dst       = 127.0.0.1   # Default destination
  \options   \
###[ ICMP ]### 
     type      = echo-request
     code      = 0
     chksum    = None
     id        = 0x0
     seq       = 0x0
     unused    = ''
```

If we get the output of the packet with `p.show2()`, the None fields get computed:
```
>>> p.show2()
###[ IP ]### 
  version   = 4
  ihl       = 5
  tos       = 0x0
  len       = 28
  id        = 1
  flags     = 
  frag      = 0
  ttl       = 64
  proto     = icmp
  chksum    = 0x7cde
  src       = 127.0.0.1
  dst       = 127.0.0.1
  \options   \
###[ ICMP ]### 
     type      = echo-request
     code      = 0
     chksum    = 0xf7ff
     id        = 0x0
     seq       = 0x0
     unused    = ''
```

Sending ICMP echo request to localhost—run `p = IP(dst="127.0.0.1")/ICMP(type="echorequest"); p.show(); ans,unans = sr(p, timeout=2)`—gives:

```
Begin emission: 
Finished sending 1 packets.
Received 127 packets, got 0 answers, remaining 1 packets
```

The emission shows the packet was sent successfully, but got 0 answers - when sending ICMP to localhost, the kernel typically handles the loopback internally without routing through the network layer where Scapy's listener sits, so no reply is captured.

```
python3 scapy/tools/UTscapy.py -t test/fields.uts -F -q
python3 scapy/tools/UTscapy.py -t test/scapy/layers/inet.uts -F -q
python3 scapy/tools/UTscapy.py -t test/scapy/layers/inet6.uts -F -q
```

IP class in scapy/layers/inet.py lines 521-537 defines defaults:

```
class IP(Packet, IPTools):
    fields_desc = [BitField("version", 4, 4),
                   BitField("ihl", None, 4),
                   XByteField("tos", 0),
                   ShortField("len", None),
                   ShortField("id", 1),
                   FlagsField("flags", 0, 3, ["MF", "DF", "evil"]),
                   BitField("frag", 0, 13),
                   ByteField("ttl", 64),
                   ByteEnumField("proto", 0, IP_PROTOS),
                   XShortField("chksum", None),
                   SourceIPField("src", "dst"),
                   DestIPField("dst", "127.0.0.1"),
                   PacketListField("options", [], IPOption, length_from=lambda p:p.ihl * 4 - 20)]
```

post_build() lines 539-551 calculates ihl/len/chksum; SourceIPField lines 854-889 auto-resolves src from routing table.
